title: Optical Mapping Preparations for Kiwifruit
author: Elena Hilario
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ggrbtv6

While waiting for the two centrifugations described above, prepare the Percoll gradients: Prepare 10 mL of 75% Percoll in NEB-A and split into two 15 mL Falcon tubes. The two tubes should weight exactly the same. Prepare 10 mL of 37.5% Percoll in NEB-A, split into 2 tubes. The two tubes should weight exactly the same. Keep both sets in the fridge until ready. The buffers used for preparing the Percoll gradients do not conain PVP-K40 because it forms a brown precipiate in the final agarose plug that prevents the DNA to migrate freely out of the matrix. However the isolated nuclei obtained in step 10 are dissolved in NEB-βME, at about 1% PVP-K40, which dilutes into the gradient buffers.
Discard 600 µL of supernatant and resuspend the nuclei in the remaining 400 µL NEB-B by tapping the bottom of the tube. Keep on ice until ready.

steps.title: Initial Tissue Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare approximately 1 g of tissue (young leaves or root tips) in Otto I buffer.

substeps.instruction: Rinse tissue thoroughly in tap water.
For leaves: Place in a 15 mL Falcon tube containing 10 mL Otto I buffer.
For root tips: Place on ~5 mL Otto I buffer in a Petri dish on ice, remove debris with a fine hair paint brush, then transfer to a Falcon tube with 10 mL Otto I buffer.

steps.title: Sample Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the sample on ice for 10 min, horizontally, with gentle shaking.

substeps.instruction: Tap the tube over the bench to release bubbles if they accumulate between leaves.
Check for bubbles halfway through the incubation.

steps.title: Tissue Chopping
steps.instruction: Transfer the sample into a Petri dish with ~5 mL of Otto I buffer inside a fume hood and finely chop the tissue into ~1 mm pieces using two scalpel blades.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize the chopped tissue using a tissue homogenizer.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the sample and buffer to the homogenizer using a spatula and disposable Pasteur pipette.
Add 5-10 mL of NEB Complete and insert the pestle.
Homogenize by pulling and pushing the pestle gently in a spiral movement just below the liquid level, avoiding foam.
If tissue remains at the bottom, use a Pasteur pipette to bring it up into the medium.

steps.title: Sample Filtration
steps.instruction: Filter the homogenized sample through Miracloth into a 50 mL Falcon tube.

substeps.instruction: Secure one sheet of Miracloth over the mouth of a 50 mL Falcon tube with rubber bands, depressing the center with a thumb.
Prewet the Miracloth with 2-3 mL NEB Complete.
Filter the sample; if flow slows, gently brush the inside of the sheet with a clean spatula.
Discard the Miracloth and adjust the final volume to 30 mL using NEB Complete.

steps.title: Detergent Addition and Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Add Triton X-100 and pellet the sample.

substeps.instruction: Add 600 µL of 25% Triton X-100 by pipetting it in a circular motion against the top inside wall of the tube.
Close the tube and mix by gently inverting about 20 times (final concentration 0.5%).
Transfer the sample to an OakRidge tube.
Spin down at 3,380 rpm (1,800 g, SS34 rotor) for 15 min at 10°C.
Spin down again as before and discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Pellet Resuspension and Sieving
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet and filter through sequential sieves.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 7 mL NEB-A by gently swirling the tube.
Assemble two 50 mL Falcon tubes with 100 µm and 40 µm sieves, respectively.
Pour the sample through the 100 µm sieve, then through the 40 µm sieve.
Keep the sample on ice.

steps.title: First Percoll Gradient Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Perform the first Percoll gradient separation to isolate nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Carefully overlay 3.5 mL of nuclei solution over each 75% Percoll solution, ensuring loaded tubes weigh exactly the same.
Spin down at 650 g for 30 min at 10°C (Acceleration = 9 max, Deceleration = 1 min).
Using a light source behind the gradient, slowly collect the sample at the interphase using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Transfer the sample to a new 15 mL Falcon tube and repeat for the second gradient tube (total sample ~4 mL).
Gently resuspend until homogeneous.

steps.title: Second Percoll Gradient Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Perform the second Percoll gradient separation.

substeps.instruction: Carefully overlay half of the sample on each 37.5% Percoll tube, ensuring tubes weigh exactly the same.
Spin down as before (650 g, 30 min at 10°C, Accel 9, Decel 1).
Remove the solution with a disposable Pasteur pipette without disturbing the small, pale yellowish nuclei pellet.

steps.title: Nuclei Washing and Concentration
steps.instruction: Wash and concentrate the nuclei pellets.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend each nuclei pellet in 10 mL NEB-B and spin down at 650 g for 30 min at 10°C (Acceleration and Deceleration both set at 9 max).
Remove the solution with a disposable Pasteur pipette, leaving ~200 µL.
Gently tap the bottom of the tube to resuspend the nuclei and transfer to a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Repeat for the second pellet.
Add ~600 µL of NEB-B and spin down at 6,000 rpm for 1 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Agarose Plug Preparation
steps.instruction: Embed the nuclei in agarose plugs.

substeps.instruction: While running Percoll gradients, place CleanCut 2% Agarose in a 70°C water bath until melted.
Transfer 400 µL of melted agarose to a screw-capped tube and keep in the water bath.
Precool one strip of disposable plug molds on ice on Parafilm.
Incubate the nuclei and the melted 2% agarose at 43°C for 10 min.
Transfer the nuclei mix to the agarose tube and mix very gently by pipetting until even.
Place the precooled plug mold on a paper towel on the bench.
Dispense ~90 µL per plug (prepare ~8 plugs).
Cool completely for 10 min on ice.

steps.title: Plug Lysis and Washing
steps.instruction: Lyse the cells and wash the agarose plugs.

substeps.instruction: Pop the agarose plugs into Proteinase K lysis mix using the plastic tab and incubate for 20 h at 50°C without shaking.
Wash plugs in 25 mL Wash-1 for 1 h at 50°C without shaking.
Wash plugs in 25 mL Wash-2 for 1 h at room temperature in a rotisserie at slowest speed.

steps.title: Plug Storage and Analysis
steps.instruction: Store and analyze the plugs via PFGE.

substeps.instruction: Store plugs in 2 mL Wash-2 at 4°C.
Analyze plugs using a 1% agarose gel (Certified™ Megabase Agarose BioRad cat #1613109) in 1X TAE.
Set PFGE parameters: 60-120", 120°, 6 V/cm, 15°C, 24 h.
Stain the gel with SybrSafe.
